subject: Synthara Health — Hosted API: Data Residency, TTL and Purge Guidance
messages:
From: Oliver Greene <oliver.greene@synthara.health>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@synthara.health
Date: 2027-01-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Synthara Q: Data residency / retention specifics for Hosted API

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — team was impressed with the latency profile. Our security and compliance group asked me to capture a short set of concrete questions about the Hosted API data lifecycle so we can sign off for a PHI-adjacent workload. Can you confirm the following points with specifics (ideally with a short timeline or pointer to evidence)?

1) Tenant pinning / regional placement: can we guarantee that requests and stored artifacts for a given tenant are pinned to a single AWS region (us-west-2) for the lifetime of the tenant?
2) Short-term artifacts: what is persisted in ephemeral caches (KV cache, prefix cache) vs durable logs? How long do caches persist after the last request?
3) Retention windows: default retention for (a) model request/response payloads, (b) audit logs and request metadata, (c) aggregate usage analytics.
4) Deletion & backups: when a tenant requests a full erasure, how do you ensure copies in snapshots/backups are also removed? Typical ask: explicit policy + expected time-to-complete.
5) Evidence: can you provide a short authoritative statement or control that we can attach to our internal risk review (SOC2, KMS usage, key destruction, and forensics readiness).

If it's easier I can share a short questionnaire; otherwise a bulletized Q&A will work. We're hoping to get a gating decision by 2027-01-20.

Appreciate it —
Oliver
Oliver Greene
Head of IT Compliance, Synthara Health
oliver.greene@synthara.health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Greene <oliver.greene@synthara.health>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-13T10:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Synthara Q: Data residency / retention specifics for Hosted API

Hi Oliver — great to meet you earlier. Below is a concise Q&A addressing the five points; I’m keeping each answer action-oriented and linking what we can provide as evidence. If you want, we can convert this into a one-page attestation for your review team.

1) Tenant pinning / regional placement
- Yes: for Hosted API customers we offer region pinning to a single AWS region (e.g., us-west-2) at onboarding. Pinning is done at the tenant control-plane level and enforced by our smart routing layer; traffic and persisted artifacts for that tenant are routed to and stored in the pinned region.
- Exceptions: disaster-recovery cross-replication can be enabled by contract; by default cross-region replication is OFF.
- Evidence: configuration screenshot / tenant metadata export available on request.

2) Short-term artifacts (ephemeral caches)
- What is cached: KV cache (model key/value cache for generation), prefix cache for repeated prompts, and short-lived CPU/GPU swap state.
- Default cache TTL: 72 hours of inactivity. Cache eviction is automatic; caches are not part of durable backups.
- Stored elsewhere: logs and request metadata (see next) are durable; ephemeral caches are purged by the runtime garbage collector and removed from disk when eviction occurs.
- Evidence: runtime cache eviction doc + data flow diagram attached.

3) Retention windows
- Model request/response payloads: default 30 days for hosted API (used for quality monitoring and safety); optional enterprise setting to 0 (no retention) at tenant creation.
- Audit logs & request metadata: 90 days by default; enterprise customers can increase via add-on or request longer-term retention for auditing purposes.
- Aggregate usage analytics: retained 24 months by default and reduced to anonymized aggregates after 90 days.
- Evidence: attached stanza-retention-policy.pdf (sections A–C).

4) Deletion & backups
- Tenant-initiated erasure: we perform the following steps once an erasure request is confirmed by the control plane: (a) mark tenant data for deletion, (b) purge active storage and caches, (c) revoke access keys and rotate KMS envelopes, (d) schedule backup sanitization.
- Backups & snapshots: snapshots are retained for a rolling 45-day period; deletion requests will be included in the next sanitization pass. Worst-case sanitization completion: 45 days from confirmed request.
- Forensic copies: if a legal hold is placed we will not delete until the hold is released; we’ll provide a written escalation path.
- Evidence: deletion playbook excerpt available; can also provide an attestation for your records.

5) Evidence & controls
- SOC 2 Type II: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II controls; we can provide the report under an NDA.
- KMS/HSM: tenant encryption handled via AWS KMS; enterprise customers may bring keys via AWS KMS or integrate with an HSM-based partner for private deployments. Key rotation and envelope wrapping are used; we can document the key destruction process for erasures.
- Forensics readiness: logs required for forensic analysis are retained per the audit log window and can be exported.

Attachments I’m including: 
- [attachment: redwood-data-flow-diagram.png (PNG, 180KB)]
- [attachment: stanza-retention-policy.pdf (PDF, 54KB)]

Next steps:
- I can assemble a short 1-page attestation (SOC2 references + TTL windows + backup sanitization timeline).
- If you need stricter timelines (e.g., <14 days for snapshot purge), we can scope as an SLA item for Dedicated or Private deployments.

Would you like the attestation + a DocuSign SLA draft for review?

Best,

Subject: Re: Synthara Q: Data residency / retention specifics for Hosted API

Thanks Vanessa — helpful summary. A couple of follow-ups from our security team, and copying Neha so Redwood can confirm internally: 

A) Snapshot sanitization timeline: your 45-day worst-case is noted. For PHI-adjacent workloads we need a contractual maximum of 30 days for complete sanitization unless an explicit legal hold exists. Can Redwood commit to 30 days as an SLA line item for our account (DEAL-9831) if we proceed?

B) Key destruction: please confirm the exact steps for KMS envelope destruction and whether Redwood can produce a time-stamped proof-of-destruction artifact (signed hash / audit event).

C) Logs export: we will need an automated export option for raw audit logs (S3-compatible export) retained for 90 days in our account, with the ability to request a one-off archive for 7 years in our environment. Can Redwood provide an S3 export hook or a managed export process?

D) Evidence format: if you can provide the attestation as a PDF and the SOC2 under NDA that will speed our internal sign-off.

Oliver — if you can confirm that these items are deal-conditional, we’ll flag for procurement to prepare PO + standard terms.

Thanks,
Priya Mehta
Manager, Information Risk & Compliance, Synthara Health
priya.mehta@synthara.health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Synthara Q: Data residency / retention specifics for Hosted API

Hi Priya / Oliver — looping in Marissa (Legal) and Neha (Security) to confirm. Short answers and commitments below; happy to iterate on contract language.

A) Snapshot sanitization SLA
- Commitment: Redwood can offer a DEAL-specific SLA to reduce snapshot sanitization worst-case to 30 days for hosted API customers as part of an annual committed contract. We will add the 30-day sanitization clause to the service schedule for DEAL-9831.

B) Key destruction / proof artifact
- Process: when a tenant erasure is executed we perform KMS envelope key revocation and rotate master keys; we then record an immutable audit event containing the envelope id(s), timestamp, and the erasure action.
- Proof: Redwood can provide a signed proof-of-destruction record (SHA256 hash of the envelope IDs + timestamp) and a copy of the corresponding audit event exported as a signed JSON file. Delivery: included as part of the erasure confirmation package.

C) Logs export to customer S3
- Supported: yes — we support scheduled or on-demand exports of raw audit logs to a customer-managed S3 bucket (customer must provide temporary write credentials scoped to an export job). We will include the export hook and a one-off archival transfer for long-term retention (your 7-year archive) as an add-on professional services item.

D) Evidence & SOC2
- We will provide: (1) a 1-page attestation PDF (signed by Redwood Security), (2) SOC 2 Type II report under NDA, and (3) the deletion playbook excerpt.

Attachments:
- [attachment: signed-sla-docusign-link.txt] (DocuSign URL included in the file)

1) Vanessa will produce the 1-page attestation + include the stanza-retention-policy excerpt in a single PDF and share.

3) Technical onboarding: Neha will coordinate with Synthara engineers for the S3 export test (suggested window: week of 2027-01-25).
